Of twelve returned jobs, ten advertise completed and two queued. Four job conclusions are success, six failure and two null. The iOS and Mac Bridges jobs have no observed steps; not all workflows are terminal and no all-required-workflow success exists.

Planning Linux, Planning Mac, Desktop/JVM KMP and Bridges Linux advertise successful job conclusions at this checkpoint. The Desktop named test/report steps advertise success; no original JUnit contents, artifact identity, distribution or loaded-artifact enrollment was inspected.

Android step 9 advertises success for host tests and clean/invalid actual Lint controls, then step 10 advertises adapter failure. No specific failure mechanism, immutable fixture-capture contents, Android device runtime execution or full Android/rule qualification is established.

All three Windows long-path and checkout steps and both relevant Mac Python harness steps advertise success. Later Windows and Implementation Mac stages fail. Narrow API step success is not a fresh unittest count, real Windows descriptor identity, native production supervision or Apple ABI proof.

The Implementation Linux tiny-native-control step advertises success, but its first failed step is build/test/assembly. API step names and conclusions alone do not prove real compiler/helper/linker execution, original control outcomes or production supervision.

No ad632ac failure logs, original reports, artifact bundles or distributions were requested or reused. Earlier b807 diagnoses and unittest counts are not attributed to these different exact-job observations; all six current failure mechanisms remain undiagnosed from metadata alone.
